title: SAMSum Corpus: A Human-annotated Dialogue Dataset for Abstractive Summarization

numbers.sentence: The dataset is freely available for the research community The dataset is shared on terms of the Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) license.
The dataset is freely available for the research community The dataset is shared on terms of the Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) license.
The results revealed that 94% of examined dialogues were classified by both annotators as good i.e. they do look like conversations from a messenger app and could be condensed in a reasonable way.

In a similar validation task, conducted for the existing dialogue-type datasets (described in the Initial approach section), the annotators agreed that only 28% of the dialogues resembled conversations from a messenger app.
Most conversations consist of dialogues between two interlocutors (about 75% of all conversations), the rest is between three or more people.
In all our experiments, news and dialogues are truncated to 400 tokens, and summaries -- to 100 tokens.

foundation.sentence: We train lightweight convolution models in two manners: (1) learning token representations from scratch; in this case we apply BPE tokenization with the vocabulary of 30K types, using fastBPE implementation[<https://github.com/glample/fastBPE>] [Sennrich et al. 2015]; (2) initializing token embeddings with pre-trained language model representations; as a language model we choose GPT-2 small [Radford et al. 2019].
foundation.title: Neural machine translation of rare words with subword units

assumptions.sentence: After collecting all of the conversations, we asked language experts to annotate them with summaries, assuming that they should (1) be rather short, (2) extract important pieces of information, (3) include names of interlocutors, (4) be written in the third person.
